is seeking a compassionate, organized, and experienced Rehabilitation Case Manager with a social work background
to support individuals and families navigating complex injuries, health challenges, and rehabilitation needs.

This position is particularly suited to a social worker who combines strong clinical insight with excellent care coordination skills. The successful candidate will understand how medical, emotional, family, financial, and environmental factors can affect recovery and participation in daily life.

Key Responsibilities

Complete comprehensive assessments of clients’ rehabilitation, psychosocial, functional, and community-support needs.
Develop individualized rehabilitation and treatment plans in collaboration with clients, families, and healthcare professionals.
Coordinate services provided by occupational therapists, physiotherapists, psychologists, social workers, speech-language pathologists, rehabilitation support workers, personal support workers, physicians, and other specialists.
Provide supportive counselling, advocacy, crisis intervention, and practical assistance to clients and families.
Facilitate referrals and help clients access appropriate medical, rehabilitation, mental-health, housing, financial, and community resources.
Attend medical appointments, treatment-team meetings, discharge-planning meetings, and case conferences as required.
Monitor clients’ progress, identify barriers to recovery, and adjust rehabilitation plans when needs change.
Maintain regular communication with clients, families, treatment providers, and other involved parties.
Prepare clear, professional clinical notes, progress reports, correspondence, treatment recommendations, and funding requests.
Review provider reports and recommendations to ensure services remain coordinated and focused on the client’s goals.
Maintain accurate documentation, service records, invoices, and time entries.
Support clients using a trauma-informed, culturally responsive, and strengths-based approach.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Social Work.
Registration and good standing with the applicable provincial College of Social Workers and Social Service Workers.
Experience in rehabilitation, healthcare, mental health, community services, hospital discharge planning, disability management, or complex case coordination.
Knowledge of acquired brain injury, spinal cord injury, chronic pain, orthopaedic injuries, psychological trauma, and cognitive or functional impairments is an asset.
Strong assessment, counselling, advocacy, crisis-management, and problem-solving skills.
Excellent written communication and clinical documentation abilities.
Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with an interdisciplinary treatment team.
Strong organization and time-management skills, with the ability to coordinate multiple priorities and deadlines.
Valid driver’s licence, reliable vehicle, and willingness to travel to clients’ homes and appointments as needed.
Experience supporting individuals following motor vehicle accidents is an asset.

The Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is empathetic without losing objectivity, confident when advocating for clients, and comfortable working with individuals and families during stressful and uncertain periods. They can see the whole person—not only the injury—and understand how relationships, mental health, finances, housing, culture, and access to support can influence recovery.
They are also a strong coordinator who follows through, communicates clearly, maintains detailed records, and helps ensure that everyone involved in the client’s rehabilitation is working toward consistent and meaningful goals.

Why Join Tri-Star?

Meaningful work supporting clients and families through complex recoveries.
A collaborative, interdisciplinary environment.
Variety and independence in day-to-day work.
Opportunities to use both social-work and case-management skills.
The ability to make a practical difference in clients’ safety, independence, and quality of life.

Qualified applicants are invited to submit a résumé and cover letter outlining their social-work, rehabilitation, and case-management experience.

new_jobs.title: After Office Hours Social Worker
new_jobs.description:
SUNY Upstate Medical University – Syracuse, NY (On-Site)

Join one of the region’s most advanced academic medical centers and help shape critical patient outcomes in a dynamic, mission-driven environment. At SUNY Upstate, your expertise is valued, your voice is heard, and your professional growth is actively supported.

As an After Office Hours Social Worker, you will provide essential care to a diverse outpatient population in our Pediatric Behavioral Health After Hours Center. This is a unique opportunity to deliver impactful services during evenings and weekends—when access to care is often most needed. You’ll work closely with patients and families to assess needs, provide intervention, and care coordination while working collaboratively with a multidisciplinary team to support the psychosocial needs of patients and their families.

What You’ll Do

Deliver behavioral health services to pediatric and adolescent patients in an after-hours setting (walk-in and call-ahead)
Conduct psychosocial assessments and provide therapeutic interventions for at-risk patients
Collaborate with a multidisciplinary team to ensure comprehensive, patient-centered care
Provide behavioral health consultations and recommendations to support treatment planning
Coordinate with the Integrated Care Manager and ancillary staff to facilitate appropriate referrals and services
Support patients and families by addressing psychosocial needs through care planning and resource connection

Minimum Qualifications

Master’s degree in Social Work (M.S.W.)
Licensed Master Social Worker (L.M.S.W.), Licensed Clinical Social Worker (L.C.S.W.), or eligibility required
3+ years of relevant post-master’s experience

Early Career Opportunity

Recent M.S.W. graduates who are L.M.S.W.-eligible are encouraged to apply! Candidates may be appointed at the entry-level (SL2) with a commensurate salary upon obtaining a Limited Permit. Licensure (L.M.S.W.) must be obtained within 12 months.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in a hospital and/or healthcare setting preferred. Experience working with the child/adolescent patient population preferred.

Work Days

Evening and weekend shifts
Monday–Friday: Between 1:00 PM – 9:30 PM
Weekends: Between 11:00 AM – 7:30 PM
Flexible scheduling within these ranges to include 1 weekend day requirement a week

Why Join SUNY Upstate?

We offer more than just a job—we provide a rewarding career with strong support and meaningful benefits:

Comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage
NYS retirement plan
Generous paid time off
A collaborative, inclusive, team-centered culture
Tuition assistance & professional development opportunities
Eligibility for student loan repayment programs through NHSC (HRSA-approved site)
Competitive salary with additional compensation included for evening and weekend shifts

Salary Range: $71,500-$89,721 (based on education and experience)

Message To Applicants

This is an on-site position based in Syracuse, NY at the Nappi Wellness Institute. If you are an experienced professional who is passionate about serving the community, working collaboratively with a diverse team, and helping to build a program from the ground up, apply today!
